settings.heading: America’s most overlooked childhood tummy trouble
settings.alt: A boy pushes peas around a full dinner plate while his mum watches
settings.text:
When your child is struggling in ways that don’t quite make sense:

  • Meltdowns over nothing
  • Living on crackers and sugar, pushing real food away
  • Restless nights and tired, grumpy mornings
  • “My tummy hurts” on repeat
  • That general feeling your kid is just… off

It’s easy to brush it off as normal kid stuff, or just a phase.

But when the same signs keep showing up and nothing you try works, it’s worth looking somewhere most parents never do: their gut.

The common kind is quiet. It’s mild, it looks like everyday childhood, and it’s almost never suspected, which is exactly why it gets missed.
settings.stat: Pinworm is the most common worm infection in the U.S.
settings.stat_note: School-aged and preschool children are the most commonly affected
settings.warn: Kids pick things up everywhere: sandpits, school bathrooms, shared toys, pets and playgrounds. And little hands go straight into little mouths.
settings.good: When their gut feels clean and settled, kids eat better, mornings get easier, and your happy, hungry kid comes back.*
settings.accordions:
🤔 Why hasn’t my pediatrician mentioned this? | Most check-ups focus on growth and milestones. Mild, everyday gut trouble rarely comes up unless a parent asks, so it’s worth raising if the signs keep showing up.
🦠 How do kids pick things up? | Through hands and mouths: school bathrooms, sandpits, shared toys, pets, playgrounds and food. It spreads easily between siblings and classmates.
👩‍⚕️ When should I see a doctor? | See your doctor if your child has ongoing or severe tummy pain, vomiting, blood in their stool, weight loss, itching around the bottom at night, or worms you can see.

settings.heading: Fits into your morning in 30 seconds
settings.alt: A dropper of ParaPatrol going into a glass of juice
settings.text:
ParaPatrol is a gentle, once-a-day dropper, not a harsh cleanse. No special diets, no days off school, no bathroom emergencies.

It mixes straight into juice, milk or a smoothie, so it slips into the school-run routine without a fight.
settings.steps:
Shake well and fill the dropper to the 1 mL line.
Mix into juice, milk or a smoothie. Orange juice and berry smoothies hide the herbal taste best.
Give once a day with food for 2–3 weeks, then take a break.

settings.heading: Your questions answered
settings.items:
What age can my child start? | ParaPatrol is made and dosed for kids 3 and up. It is not for children under 3.
How fast will I see a difference? | Every child is different. Many parents notice settled tummies and better appetites within 1–2 weeks of daily use.*
What does it taste like? | A natural raspberry flavour with a bitter blocker to soften the herbal taste. Mixed into orange juice or a berry smoothie, most kids drink it without a fuss.
Is it safe? What about side effects? | Stop use and talk to your doctor if your child has vomiting, diarrhea, stomach pain or any unusual reaction. Start with half a dropper for the first few days if your child has a sensitive tummy.
Can we use it with other supplements or medication? | If your child takes medication or has a health condition, talk to your pediatrician first. Bring the bottle so they can see the full ingredient list.
What if my child has a nut allergy? | ParaPatrol contains tree nut (black walnut), so it is not for kids with a tree nut allergy.
Does it contain alcohol or sugar? | No alcohol and no sugar. It is also gluten-free.
What if we miss a day? | Just carry on the next day with the usual dose. Don’t double up.
How does the guarantee work? | Try ParaPatrol for 30 days. If you’re not happy, contact our team and we’ll refund you.
How long does shipping take? | Orders are usually processed within 1–2 business days and most arrive within 7–15 days. Shipping is free on every order.
